Predictions for flexCountReg models

predict.flexCountReg.Rd

Generates predictions for the expected count (lambda) for observations.

For countreg.rp (Random Parameters) models, three methods are available:

  • Simulated: Uses Halton draws to simulate the random parameters and averages the outcomes. This is a simulation-based approximation.

  • Individual (alias EB): Empirical Bayes observation-specific predictions (Wood and Gayah, 2025, Eqs. 5-7). Each simulation draw is weighted by the likelihood of the unit's observed outcomes (all of a panel's rows when panel_id was used), giving conditional coefficients \(E[\beta_i | y_i]\). By default these are used in the mean function, as in the paper; pass eb_type = "mean" to instead return the conditional mean \(E[\mu_{it} | y_i]\). The conditional coefficients and their conditional standard deviations are returned as the attributes "eb_coefficients" and "eb_sd". Requires the outcome (and the panel_id column, if used) in newdata, so it is meant for data with observed outcomes.

  • Exact: Uses the moment generating functions (MGFs) of the random parameter distributions (Wood and Gayah, 2025, Appendix A), including heterogeneity in means and variances. This is exact for normal, uniform, triangular and gamma parameters and has no simulation error. For lognormal parameters it uses a Laplace (saddlepoint) approximation, which is accurate for \(x < 0\); for \(x > 0\) (and for gamma parameters with \(x\sigma^2/\mu \ge 1\)) the expected value is infinite and Inf is returned with a warning.

For countreg, poisLindRE, and RENB models, the function calculates the expected value \(\mu = \exp(X\beta)\) (with appropriate adjustments for specific families like PLN, PLL or underreporting).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  ...,
  type = c("response", "true", "prob_reported", "link", "prob", "zero"),
  new_data = NULL
)

Arguments

object

a model object estimated using this R package.

newdata

optional data frame for which to generate predictions. It must contain every variable used by the model's formulas (including rpar_formula, dis_param_formula_1/2, underreport_formula and heterogeneity formulas) and any offset columns. The outcome is not required. If omitted, predictions are made for the data used to fit the model.

...

optional arguments passed to the function. This includes method. Passing the data as data = is deprecated; use newdata.

type

the type of prediction. "response" (default) is the expected observed count. For models with underreporting this is \(\mu \times p\), the true mean times the probability of being reported. "true" is the true expected count \(\mu\) (excluding the underreporting probability), "prob_reported" is the probability of being reported \(p\), and "link" is the linear predictor \(X\beta\) plus the offset. For models without underreporting, "true" equals "response" and "prob_reported" is 1. For zero-inflated and hurdle models (zero_formula), "response" includes the zero model, "true" is the mean of the count distribution alone, and "zero" is the probability from the zero model: the probability of a structural zero (zero-inflated) or of a zero count (hurdle). "prob" returns a matrix of probabilities \(P(Y = k)\) with one row per row of newdata and one column per count \(k = 0, \dots,\) max_count (passed in ...; default the largest count in the training data), for rootograms and for scoring models out of sample. Types other than "response" are available for countreg models only.

new_data

the same as newdata, under the name used by tidymodels. Give one or the other.

Value

A numeric vector of predicted expected counts for each observation in the provided data. If no data is provided, the predictions for the data used in estimating the model are provided.

Details

The returned vector always has one element per row of newdata, in the same order. Rows with missing values in any variable the model uses get NA. Factor levels and contrasts from the training data are used, so newdata may contain only a subset of the levels. An error is raised if an offset column is missing from newdata.

Note

optional parameter method: Only valid for random parameters models (countreg.rp). Options include Simulated (default), Individual (or EB), or Exact.

optional parameter eb_type: for method = "Individual", either "coefficients" (default) or "mean".

References

Wood, J.S., Gayah, V. (2025). Out-of-sample prediction and interpretation for random parameter generalized linear models. Accident Analysis and Prevention, 220, 108147.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Load data and create a dummy variable
data("washington_roads")
washington_roads$AADT10kplus <- ifelse(washington_roads$AADT > 10000, 1, 0)

# =========================================================================
# 1. Fixed Parameter Model (countreg)
# =========================================================================
nb2_fixed <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50,
                      data = washington_roads, 
                      family = "NB2")
pred_fixed <- predict(nb2_fixed, newdata = washington_roads)

# =========================================================================
# 2. Random Parameters Model (countreg.rp)
# =========================================================================
rp_nb2 <- countreg.rp(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                      rpar_formula = ~ -1 + speed50,
                      data = washington_roads,
                      family = "NB2",
                      rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"),
                      ndraws = 100)

# Method A: Simulated (Default)
pred_sim <- predict(rp_nb2, newdata = washington_roads, method = "Simulated")

# Method B: Exact (Analytical MGF)
pred_exact <- predict(rp_nb2, newdata = washington_roads, method = "Exact")

# Method C: Individual (Empirical Bayes, requires the observed outcome)
pred_eb <- predict(rp_nb2, newdata = washington_roads, method = "Individual")

# =========================================================================
# 3. Random Effects Models (poisLindRE / RENB)
# =========================================================================
pl_re <- poisLind.re(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                     data = washington_roads,
                     group_var = "ID")
pred_pl_re <- predict(pl_re, newdata = washington_roads)
# }
